claims.text: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys can exist in high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Using machine learning and molecular dynamics as an advanced-computation intervention can overcome limitations in thermodynamic-property determination for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The intervention can improve the accuracy of melting-temperature predictions relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The intervention can improve determination of enthalpy and entropy of fusion relative to current methods.
The intervention can improve determination of volume change upon melting relative to current methods.
The intervention can improve determination of liquid thermodynamic properties relative to current methods.
The intervention can increase the availability of the listed thermodynamic-property data.
The intervention can increase the efficiency of determining the listed thermodynamic properties.
The proposed computational approach is applicable across a large compositional space of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Configurational entropy is a thermodynamic mediator relevant to the proposed prediction mechanism.
Mixing enthalpy is a mediator in the proposed prediction mechanism.
Gibbs free energy is a mediator in the proposed prediction mechanism.
High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal components.
Accurately accounting for complex interactions among multiple components enables accurate prediction of high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties.
Current experimental and computational methods have limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency for determining the listed properties.
The accuracy of the proposed computational methods depends on the quality of their input data.
The accuracy of the proposed computational methods depends on the complexity of interactions among alloy components.
